title: Encryption & Access Controls ops review with Helios Oncology
summary: Customer seeks assurance on end-to-end encryption, BYOK and HSM support, auditability for SOC 2, and integration patterns for Private (VPC) deployment. Discussed envelope encryption, key wrapping, HSM connectors, separation of duties, and proposed pilot with a test HSM and SOC2 artifacts.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jamie (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood Solutions Architect); Dr. Priya Rao (Helios Head of Security), Marcus Chen (Platform Lead), Lena Ortiz (Compliance), Samuel Ng (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Helios is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting for PHI-adjacent oncology analytics. Focus areas: encryption at rest/in transit, BYOK & HSM, audit logs, SSO/RBAC, data residency.

00:00:02 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call and then we'll jump into the technical items around encryption and keys.
00:00:10 Dr. Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here. we'll be focusing on our security requirements — SOC 2 controls, and how keys are handled.
00:00:18 Alex: Great — before we start, high level agenda: cover TLS/mTLS, at-rest encryption, BYOK approaches, HSM integration patterns, and then next steps. Jamie will go through the connector design.
00:00:30 Jamie (SE): Hi all. just to set context: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments. for Helios we know data sensitivity is high — you mentioned PHI-adjacent metadata, yes?
00:00:41 Dr. Priya Rao: Correct. not strictly PHI in every payload but some job results will include identifiers. we need encryption guarantees and audit trails.
00:00:50 Marcus Chen: Also we're strict on key control — must support customer-supplied keys with HSM-backed root keys.
00:01:00 Jamie: Totally. there are a couple of common patterns: 1) envelope encryption with customer master key in HSM (BYOK), 2) Redwood-managed keys with key-wrapping by customer HSM, or 3) full on-prem HSM where only wrapped keys are stored by Redwood. we recommend envelope for performance.
00:01:20 Dr. Priya Rao: Can you explain envelope encryption quickly? we want to be clear on where plaintext keys live.
00:01:25 Jamie: Sure — we encrypt objects with ephemeral data keys (DEKs). the DEKs are themselves encrypted — wrapped — by a customer master key (CMK) that lives in an HSM or cloud KMS. Redwood stores only the wrapped DEKs. decryption requires unwrapping via the customer's KMS/HSM which can be proxied during inference, or a short-lived token if you allow Redwood to call your KMS.
00:01:48 Lena Ortiz: So with envelope, Redwood never sees the CMK in plaintext, right?
00:01:52 Jamie: Correct. Redwood never has the CMK plaintext. We may hold wrapped DEKs and the runtime can unwrap them if the HSM/KMS is reachable and the customer gives permission via a signed ephemeral grant.
00:02:05 Samuel Ng: There's latency concerns if we need to call our HSM on every inference call. how does Redwood handle that?
00:02:11 Ravi (Solutions Arch): Good question. typical approach: unwrap once per worker and keep DEK in memory (KV cache) with TTL tied to token lifetime and strict memory zeroing. Redwood's runtime supports secure in-memory caching of DEKs and periodic rotation. So you don't call the KMS per request, just on cache miss or rotation.
00:02:32 Dr. Priya Rao: Is that audited? we need audit logs showing unwrap operations, who performed them, and the key version.
00:02:38 Jamie: Yes — we emit audit events for unwrap/rotate/use with timestamps, workspace, token id and the key version metadata. the payload won't include key material. logs are stored in our immutable audit store; retention configurable for enterprise.
00:02:52 Lena Ortiz: retention options? we need 7 years for some studies.
00:02:56 Alex: We can support extended retention as an add-on — we'll include that in the next steps.
00:03:02 Marcus Chen: Let's get into HSM specifics — we run a cloud HSM (PKCS#11 interface) and also have an on-prem appliance in EU for residency. can Redwood connect to both?
00:03:13 Jamie: Yes — we have two supported integration modes: 1) direct KMS API calls (Cloud HSM/Cloud KMS) where Redwood holds a short-lived credential to call your KMS in your VPC, and 2) an HSM proxy connector where you run a small agent in your VPC that Redwood calls over a mutually authenticated TLS channel; the agent performs unwraps. The second avoids exposing KMS credentials to Redwood.
00:03:37 Samuel Ng: That HSM proxy — is that open-source? what's the attack surface?
00:03:41 Jamie: The agent is customer-deployed code; we have a reference implementation. it's minimal: accepts signed requests, validates signatures, calls the PKCS#11 library to unwrap/wrap, and returns wrapped DEKs. It logs audits locally and streams metadata to Redwood's control plane over an authenticated channel. We'll share the repo.
00:04:00 Dr. Priya Rao: Audit streaming — does that include plaintext? we can't have key material in telemetry.
00:04:05 Jamie: No plaintext. The agent only sends event metadata: operation type (unwrap/wrap), key id, key version, timestamp, requester id. No key material.
00:04:15 Marcus Chen: For the private deployment (VPC), what's the control plane visibility? We're worried about management plane calls leaving the VPC.
00:04:23 Ravi: For Private, Redwood offers a customer-managed control plane option. control-plane telemetry can be routed via a relay you host. we can also support an air-gapped on-prem package. For your EU HSM we can ensure key operations remain within EU region and the agent never crosses jurisdictions.
00:04:40 Lena Ortiz: Regarding compliance docs — we need SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 scope, pen test. can you provide those?
00:04:46 Alex: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 report and pen test summary. note: pen test redacted for customer details but will include findings and remediation.
00:04:55 Dr. Priya Rao: On RBAC and SSO: we require SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO, with role-based policies that map to key access. can Redwood map roles so only certain users can trigger unwrapping or roll keys?
00:05:07 Jamie: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is fine-grained. We can map roles to KMS permissions and record which user initiated a key operation in the audit logs. We also support Just-In-Time admin elevation flows if you require MFA for key operations.
00:05:22 Samuel Ng: Do you support per-tenant key separation? we want tenant isolation.
00:05:26 Jamie: Yes — we support per-customer CMKs and per-tenant DEKs. Multi-tenant instances can be configured so that keys are scoped and cannot be used across tenants.
00:05:35 Marcus Chen: What about key rotation policies? automated? manual?
00:05:39 Jamie: We support scheduled automated rotation with policy windows, and manual rotation triggers. rotations generate new key versions; we keep old versions for decryption for a configurable window. rotations are audited and can optionally require dual-approval.
00:05:51 Dr. Priya Rao: Dual-approval — do you have a workflow?
00:05:54 Jamie: We have an approval workflow in the console that integrates with SSO. You can require two distinct principals to approve a rotation or an unseal/unwrap operation. Approvals are logged.
00:06:05 Lena Ortiz: For data-in-transit, we're standard TLS 1.3, but we want mTLS between Redwood runtime and our VPC endpoints. is that supported?
00:06:12 Ravi: Yes, mTLS supported for the HSM proxy and for private endpoints. We recommend mutual TLS to authenticate both sides, combined with network-level ACLs in your VPC.
00:06:24 Marcus Chen: If we do hosted mode initially, is there a way to bring keys later for a migration without re-encrypting everything?
00:06:30 Jamie: We support key wrapping migration — you can bring a new CMK and request Redwood to rewrap stored DEKs with the new CMK in a single background job. That avoids re-encrypting object payloads.
00:06:41 Samuel Ng: Are the wrapped DEKs portable if we want to move to another vendor?
00:06:44 Jamie: Wrapped DEKs follow standard formats; if both parties support the same wrapping algorithm and key formats, they are portable. we'll provide key export guidance.
00:06:55 Dr. Priya Rao: For evidence during audits, can you provide a chain of custody for key operations and role-attribution?
00:07:02 Alex: Yes — audit records include operation, actor (SSO id), workspace, job id, key id/version, and a cryptographic signature of the log entry for tamper evidence. We can export logs to your SIEM (S3, Splunk, or via syslog).
00:07:18 Lena Ortiz: Exported logs — can we enforce immutability and WORM?
00:07:22 Jamie: Yes — when pushed to S3 we can set object lock and retention policies. For customers requiring WORM within their environment, the HSM agent can write records locally with immutability controls.
00:07:34 Marcus Chen: Any constraints on algorithms? We require AES-GCM 256 for data keys and RSA-PSS for signing.
00:07:41 Jamie: We support AES-256-GCM for DEKs and RSA-PSS and ECDSA for signatures. For wrapping, we support AES-KW and RSA-OAEP depending on your KMS capabilities.
00:07:53 Samuel Ng: What about FIPS or HSM module attestation?
00:07:56 Jamie: We can accept FIPS-validated HSMs. for attestation, the agent can provide attestation metadata (serial, firmware version). we also support integration with HSM vendors' attestation APIs when available.
00:08:08 Dr. Priya Rao: We operate in EU and US. can you guarantee that keys for EU data stay in EU?
00:08:14 Ravi: Yes — data residency policies allow routing key operations to region-specific KMS/HSM endpoints and the HSM agent can be region-locked. we'll document the routing rules.
00:08:25 Lena Ortiz: We need an escalation path in case of key compromise. what's the runbook?
00:08:29 Alex: Our proposed runbook: 1) immediate key revoke/rotation, 2) containerized rewrap job to rotate DEKs, 3) incident analysis with timeline and audit export, 4) customer notification and remediation steps. We'll include a draft runbook as part of the deliverables.
00:08:46 Dr. Priya Rao: About key escrow — we prefer no escrow. do you require escrow?
00:08:50 Jamie: No escrow required. if you want complete custody, choose the HSM proxy mode or on-prem private deployment so Redwood never holds the means to unwrap CMKs.
00:08:59 Marcus Chen: On governance: can we enforce separation of duties for key creation vs operations?
00:09:04 Jamie: Yes — RBAC policies can separate key creation, key rotation, and unwrap privileges. Those policies map to SAML groups and SCIM provisioning.
00:09:12 Samuel Ng: For the bench session — we'll simulate loads and ensure unwraps don't become a hot path. any tooling you recommend?
00:09:18 Ravi: We'll provide a benchmark harness that simulates DEK cache churn and measures latency under load. It will include metrics for unwrap frequency, KMS calls, and memory residency.
00:09:29 Lena Ortiz: Anything on encryption of logs themselves?
00:09:33 Jamie: Audit logs at rest are encrypted with a customer-scoped key. If you bring your own key, we can use it to encrypt those logs as well.
00:09:40 Dr. Priya Rao: Any known gaps? be candid.
00:09:44 Alex: For high-compliance customers we recommend private deployment with the HSM agent. Hosted with BYOK is good but still requires a trust model for the control plane. If you need absolute separation, the on-prem package is the only zero-trust option.
00:09:58 Marcus Chen: Understood.
00:10:00 Alex: Ok let's recap and action items — we'll send SOC2, HSM connector code, schedule bench, and produce runbook and data residency doc.
00:10:10 Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks, that sounds good.
00:10:12 Jamie: quick note — I'll include a section in the connector doc about hazard scenarios and recommended limits for DEK TTLs and cache eviction to meet your audit windows.
00:10:22 Samuel Ng: I'll create the test VPC and invite Redwood.
00:10:25 Alex: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. thanks everyone.

00:26:12 Alex: We can support freeze flags for retention windows and hold states. That can be gated by two-party approval.

00:29:27 Jamie: Model artifacts can be encrypted with the same envelope model. snapshots are immutable objects; rewrap is the recommended migration path. also, the runtime can mount decrypted model weights into ephemeral memory only.

00:33:20 Alex: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with docs.
